facts.raw_span: A Chinese woman in her late 20s presented with a 20-year history of progressive skin laxity
asymptomatic yellowish coalesced papules confined to flexural areas
severe skin sagging occurred on her abdomen with loss of elasticity
no extracutaneous involvement
born to healthy nonconsanguineous parents
younger sister had developed the same skin symptoms
Thick and leathery skinfolds on the neck, axillae, inguinal regions, abdomen, and limbs, with yellowish papules scattered on the dorsal neck
Low clotting activity of factor X (52.2%; reference range, 77%-131%)
Prolonged prothrombin time (12.8 seconds; reference range, 10.4-12.6 seconds)
excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments scattered in the reticular dermis (von Kossa staining)
compound heterozygous sequence variation in GGCX gene
c.1167_1172delCTGGACinsGGGAA (p. Asn389Lys fs*13) in exon 8

concepts.why: The patient's progressive skin laxity, yellowish coalesced papules, and excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments are characteristic of pseudoxanthoma elasticum.
The patient's severe skin sagging, loss of elasticity, and family history of similar skin symptoms are consistent with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
The patient's low clotting activity of factor X and prolonged prothrombin time suggest a factor X deficiency.
The patient's progressive skin laxity and loss of elasticity are consistent with cutis laxa.
The patient's compound heterozygous sequence variation in the GGCX gene is consistent with GGCX-related pseudoxanthoma elasticum.
The patient's progressive skin laxity and yellowish coalesced papules could be consistent with acquired pseudoxanthoma elasticum, although the genetic findings suggest a genetic etiology.
The patient's yellowish coalesced papules and skin laxity could be consistent with elastosis perforans serpiginosa, although the genetic findings suggest a different diagnosis.
The patient's excessive calcification of elastic fiber fragments and skin laxity could be consistent with perforating calcific elastosis, although the genetic findings suggest a different diagnosis.
